title: Matthew 25:14-30 — The Parable of the Talents
description: A Back to the Bible study on faithfulness with what God has given — gifts, time, opportunities, and calling.
author: ROLCC Fellowship Team

sections.heading: Observe
sections.body: A master going on a journey entrusted his servants with talents — five to one, two to another, and one to a third, each according to his ability. The first two servants traded faithfully and doubled what they received. The third servant dug a hole and hid his talent. When the master returned, the faithful servants were praised: "Well done, good and faithful servant." The unfaithful servant acted from fear, blamed the master, and returned only what he had been given. The master called him wicked and lazy, took the talent away, and gave it to the one who had ten.

sections.heading: Interpret
sections.body: God gives every person gifts, abilities, opportunities, and responsibilities — and He expects faithfulness, not comparison. The servant with two talents received the same praise as the one with five because God measures faithfulness, not amount. Fear buried the third servant's potential. One day we will give account to God for how we stewarded what He entrusted to us. Faithfulness in little leads to greater responsibility; neglect brings loss. To everyone who has, more will be given — but gifts unused can become opportunities lost.

sections.heading: Apply
sections.body: Sometimes we want reward without responsibility, harvest without work, or promotion without faithfulness. God calls us to use our gifts, time, money, talents, opportunities, and spiritual calling for His glory. Fear and laziness can prevent spiritual growth. Ask yourself honestly: what has God given you, and are you using it or hiding it?

discussionQuestions: What talents has God given you?
Are you using or hiding your gifts?
Are you faithful in small things?
What can you invest for God's kingdom today?

quiz.question: How many talents did the first faithful servant receive?
quiz.explanation: The master gave five talents to the first servant according to his ability.

quiz.question: What did the servant with one talent do?
options: He hid it in the ground
He gave it to the poor
quiz.explanation: Fear led him to bury his talent instead of using it.

quiz.question: What did the master say to the faithful servants?
options: Well done, good and faithful servant
Return what you were given only
quiz.explanation: Both faithful servants heard the same praise despite different amounts.

quiz.question: What kept the unfaithful servant from acting?
quiz.explanation: He acted from fear and blamed the master.

quiz.question: What does this parable teach about stewardship?
options: God expects faithfulness with what He gives
God only rewards the most gifted
quiz.explanation: Faithfulness in little leads to greater responsibility.
